name: Axis Bank
summary:
Axis Bank is India's third-largest private sector bank, founded in 1994 following India's 1991 economic liberalization that permitted new private bank licenses for the first time since 1969. Originally named UTI Bank (sponsored by the Unit Trust of India), the bank was rebranded as Axis Bank in 2007 and has grown through organic growth and acquisitions to serve 50+ million customers across India and internationally.

Axis Bank's founding reflects the 1991 liberalization moment: Prime Minister Narasimha Rao and Finance Minister Manmohan Singh's structural adjustment program opened the Indian economy after decades of protectionism, and new private bank licenses were one of the earliest reforms. Axis Bank, HDFC Bank, and ICICI Bank — all founded in the 1994 wave — transformed Indian banking by bringing professional management, technology investment, and customer service standards absent from the state-owned banks that dominated Indian finance.

Axis Bank's 2022 acquisition of Citibank India's consumer business for $1.6 billion — the largest bank acquisition in India for years — extended Axis's premium consumer banking and credit card portfolio. The bank operates 4,900 branches and 17,000 ATMs across India, with international offices in Singapore, DIFC (Dubai), London, and Hong Kong serving NRI (non-resident Indian) customers.
